questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: You must use your turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel sharply to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently brake to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down by gently braking. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risk of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks by telling people you are driving.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it hard to make safe choices after drinking starts.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, signal and enter at the same speed as other cars. Always yield to other traffic when entering a roadway.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less when you drink beer instead of wine.
Less when you drink wine instead of beer.
Most when you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter—only how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, after the train has passed.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, when other drivers do it.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train's horn. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers rules they must follow. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: When you drive fast on wet roads, your tires cannot push water away. They lose grip and slide on the water instead. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When should you drive in a lane with a red X light?

options.text: If no cars are coming the other way.
If you are passing another car.

questions.explanation: A red X light means that lane is closed. Traffic direction in that lane changes throughout the day. Never drive in a lane with a red X.

questions.question: What might happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol's effect may become weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with cold medicine might affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you must stop at least 15 feet from the tracks. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of a train before you proceed.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include beer, wine, liquor, illegal drugs, prescription medicines, over-the-counter medicines, and inhalants.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas. Do not brake until you have control. Then brake gently and move to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: If your power steering stops working, you should:

options.text: Honk and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer hard, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer hard, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, steering will be harder. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Keep going unless cars or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going unless cars or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and cars already in the intersection go first. You can proceed, but drive at a speed you can slow down from if the light changes before you get there.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that traffic only moves in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive at a speed above 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep impairs driving the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours affects driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: Stop signs are always octagonal (eight-sided). This shape is used only for stop signs.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to signal a turn?
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when your turn signals do not work. Hand signals tell other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done as much as you can.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: If you cannot merge safely, should you stop even when a yield sign tells you to yield?
questions.explanation: When you must yield, you should also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther behind other vehicles. Your car will take longer to stop.
